author: Old North News
title: Cary announces free outdoor summer concert series at local parks and venues
text:
Cary announced on May 27 the lineup for four free outdoor live music series taking place this summer across various parks and the Page-Walker Arts & History Center. The events, which are open to the public, will feature live music performances, food trucks, craft beverages, and activities for families.
The Bands, Bites, and Boats series will be held at Bond Park Boathouse on select Fridays from May through October. Attendees can enjoy live music acts such as LaureNicole Duo on June 5, Garland Mason on July 10, Adam Pitts on August 7, My Cousin Skinny on September 4, and Amanda Peach Duo on October 2. After-hours boat rentals will also be available during these events.
The Summer Vibes series brings concerts to three neighborhood parks: Neighborhood Park at Carpenter Fire Station Road hosts Adam Decker Band on June 17; Jack Smith Park features Island Time Band on July 15; and North Cary Park presents Night Shift on August 19. Each show runs from 6 to 8 p.m., with children’s craft activities offered at each location.
Downtown Cary Park’s Great Lawn & Pavilion will host the CaryLIVE! concert series featuring regional and nationally recognized artists every Saturday evening from May through August. The schedule includes Fancy Gap opening the season May 30, Abraham Alexander performing June 27, The Suitcase Junket playing July 25, and Delta Rae closing out August 22. All CaryLIVE! concerts include an opening act.
Performances at the Page take place in the Page-Walker garden with Jamrock scheduled for June 12 and Redbud for July 31. The Redbud event is presented in partnership with PineCone Bluegrass Jam Camp and features an opening performance by student musicians. Both shows are family-friendly with food trucks available.
Concerts are scheduled to proceed sprinkle or shine; however, residents are encouraged to check the Cary Weather Delays & Cancellations webpage for updates in case of inclement weather.
